arguments.content:
#!/bin/sh
# Nightly log backup. Bundles logs/ into a dated tarball and copies it to the
# backup destination.
#
# The destination is environment-specific and is not something this repo can
# hardcode safely, so it is supplied at run time via the BACKUP_DEST
# environment variable (or a /etc/backup.conf file as a fallback). Whoever
# schedules the nightly cron job must set one of these. Supported forms:
#   - a local directory:         /mnt/backups
#   - a remote scp target:       user@host:/path/to/backups
#   - a remote rsync target:     user@host:/path/to/backups  (rsync used if available)
#
# Example cron setup:
#   BACKUP_DEST=/mnt/backups /work/backup.sh
# or put a single line in /etc/backup.conf:
#   BACKUP_DEST=/mnt/backups

set -eu

CONF_FILE="/etc/backup.conf"
if [ -z "${BACKUP_DEST:-}" ] && [ -f "$CONF_FILE" ]; then
    # shellcheck disable=SC1090
    . "$CONF_FILE"
fi

DEST="${BACKUP_DEST:-}"

if [ -z "$DEST" ]; then
    echo "backup.sh: no backup destination configured." >&2
    echo "Set the BACKUP_DEST environment variable or add it to $CONF_FILE" >&2
    echo "e.g. BACKUP_DEST=/mnt/backups or BACKUP_DEST=user@host:/path" >&2
    exit 1
fi

STAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d)
BUNDLE="logs-$STAMP.tar.gz"

tar -czf "$BUNDLE" logs/
echo "wrote $BUNDLE"

case "$DEST" in
    *:*)
        # Remote target (user@host:/path). Prefer rsync if available, fall
        # back to scp.
        if command -v rsync >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            rsync -a "$BUNDLE" "$DEST/"
        else
            scp "$BUNDLE" "$DEST/"
        fi
        ;;
    *)
        # Local path or mount point.
        mkdir -p "$DEST"
        cp "$BUNDLE" "$DEST/"
        ;;
esac

echo "copied $BUNDLE to $DEST"

arguments.command:
chmod +x backup.sh
# sanity check: missing dest should fail loudly
if ./backup.sh 2>err.txt; then echo "unexpected success"; else echo "failed as expected:"; cat err.txt; fi
rm -f logs-*.tar.gz err.txt
echo ---
mkdir -p /tmp/backup_dest
BACKUP_DEST=/tmp/backup_dest ./backup.sh
ls -la /tmp/backup_dest
rm -rf /tmp/backup_dest logs-*.tar.gz
sh -n backup.sh && echo "syntax OK"
